items.stem: What is a disadvantage of tidal barrages?

items.answer: They flood estuary habitats used by birds and fish
items.markingKey: B. High building cost too.

items.stem: Hana writes: "Renewable resources have no environmental impact." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: They affect landscapes, wildlife, land use and need materials such as metals for turbines and panels.
items.markingKey: They affect landscapes, wildlife, land use and need materials such as metals for turbines and panels. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why gas-fired power stations are often used to balance supply and demand.
items.answer: They can start up and change output quickly, unlike nuclear or coal stations.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: They can start up and change output quickly, unlike nuclear or coal stations. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

3 | 40.2 | 40.8 | 41.6

Calculate the mean power output when the hours after sunrise was 6 h.

items.stem: Arjun wants to find out how the number of blades on a model wind turbine affects its power output. Write a focused research question for this investigation that names both the independent and the dependent variable.
items.answer: How does number of blades affect power output?
items.markingKey: 1 mark: names the independent variable (number of blades (2, 3, 4, 6)); 1 mark: names the measurable dependent variable (power output = V²/R across a fixed 10 Ω resistor) in a question form.

items.stem: Evaluate the suitability of wind, solar, nuclear and gas for supplying a large city’s electricity, considering reliability, cost, emissions and environmental impact.
items.answer: Wind: cheap, renewable, no CO₂, intermittent, needs land/sea and storage. Solar: cheap, modular, only daytime, seasonal. Nuclear: reliable base load, very low CO₂, expensive and slow to build, waste and risk. Gas: flexible, reliable, cheaper to build, but CO₂ and finite. Best: mix – renewables for bulk energy, storage and some flexible low-carbon or gas backup, possibly nuclear base load.
items.markingKey: Wind: cheap, renewable, no CO₂, intermittent, needs land/sea and storage. Solar: cheap, modular, only daytime, seasonal. Nuclear: reliable base load, very low CO₂, expensive and slow to build, waste and risk. Gas: flexible, reliable, cheaper to build, but CO₂ and finite. Best: mix – renewables for bulk energy, storage and some flexible low-carbon or gas backup, possibly nuclear base load.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Storing surplus electricity, e.g. pumped hydro or batteries, to use when demand is high"?
items.answer: energy storage
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of energy storage.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "non-renewable resource"?
options: The variation in output of resources such as wind and solar that depend on weather and time of day
An energy resource that is replenished naturally on a human timescale, e.g. solar, wind, hydro, tidal, geothermal, biomass
An energy resource that will run out, e.g. coal, oil, natural gas, uranium
Reliable access to affordable energy, without depending on unstable supplies
items.answer: An energy resource that will run out, e.g. coal, oil, natural gas, uranium
items.markingKey: C. "non-renewable resource" is an energy resource that will run out, e.g. coal, oil, natural gas, uranium.

items.stem: Explain the difference between solar power and wind power.
items.answer: Wind power uses moving air to turn turbines, works day and night but varies with wind speed; solar power uses photovoltaic cells (or heat), only works in daylight and varies with cloud cover and season.
items.markingKey: Wind power uses moving air to turn turbines, works day and night but varies with wind speed; solar power uses photovoltaic cells (or heat), only works in daylight and varies with cloud cover and season. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims: "Renewable resources have no environmental impact." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: They affect landscapes, wildlife, land use and need materials such as metals for turbines and panels.
items.markingKey: They affect landscapes, wildlife, land use and need materials such as metals for turbines and panels. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why nuclear power is non-renewable but low-carbon.
items.answer: Uranium is a finite resource, but fission produces no CO₂, so emissions come only from construction, mining and processing.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Uranium is a finite resource, but fission produces no CO₂, so emissions come only from construction, mining and processing. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.answer: New wind and solar are now often the cheapest electricity, but costs depend on location, storage and grid needs.

items.answer: 45%; it produces nothing at night and less on cloudy days and in winter

items.stem: Using Germany’s Energiewende as an example, explain balancing an energy transition.
items.answer: Germany expanded wind and solar to over 40% of electricity and phased out nuclear in 2023, but relied on coal and gas for backup during the transition. Shows the challenges of intermittency, costs and policy trade-offs.

items.stem: "Wind farms should be built in national parks if they are the windiest locations." To what extent is this view justified?
items.answer: National parks should generally be protected; offshore and less sensitive windy sites should be prioritised.

items.stem: Write a risk assessment for an investigation into how the number of blades on a model wind turbine affects its power output. Identify two hazards, the risk each poses and how each risk will be reduced, and explain one ethical or environmental consideration.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "cooling tower"?
options: A set of blades turned by steam, water or wind that drives a generator
A device that uses electromagnetic induction to convert kinetic energy into electrical energy
A structure that condenses steam back into water by transferring thermal energy to the air
Reliable access to affordable energy, without depending on unstable supplies
items.answer: A structure that condenses steam back into water by transferring thermal energy to the air
items.markingKey: C. "cooling tower" is a structure that condenses steam back into water by transferring thermal energy to the air.

items.stem:
Kenji compared the efficiency of power stations commissioned in different decades using published data (three stations per decade).

Year commissioned | Efficiency / %: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
1960 | 28 | 29 | 27
1975 | 35 | 36 | 35
1990 | 43 | 42 | 44
2005 | 50 | 51 | 49
2020 | 60 | 59 | 57

Describe the trend shown by the results and explain it using scientific knowledge.
items.answer: Power station efficiency has increased steadily over time. Newer stations use higher steam temperatures and pressures, better turbine design and combined-cycle gas turbines, so a larger fraction of the fuel energy becomes electrical energy.
items.markingKey: 1 trend: Power station efficiency has increased steadily over time.; 1 use of data (quote means/values); 1-2 explanation: Newer stations use higher steam temperatures and pressures, better turbine design and combined-cycle gas turbines, so a larger fraction of the fuel energy becomes electrical energy.

items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "Old coal power stations should be converted to burn biomass (wood pellets)."
items.answer: Conversion can be a short-term step, but only with sustainably sourced local biomass; it is not a long-term solution.

items.stem: Describe how a gas-fired power station generates electricity, draw (describe) a Sankey diagram for a 40% efficient station with 1000 MJ input, and suggest two ways to improve its efficiency.
items.answer: Gas burns in a boiler → heats water → high-pressure steam → turbine spins → generator (coil in magnetic field) → electricity; steam condensed in cooling towers. Improvements: combined-cycle gas turbine; CHP to use waste heat; better insulation/maintenance.

items.stem: A 2000 MW power station burning natural gas (energy density 55 MJ/kg) is 33% efficient. Calculate the mass of fuel burned per day in tonnes.
items.answer: 9521 tonnes
items.markingKey: M1 input power = 2000 ÷ 0.33 = 6061 MW; M1 energy per day = 6061 × 3600 × 24 = 5.24 × 10^8 MJ; M1 mass = ÷ 55 MJ/kg = 9.52 × 10^6 kg; A1 9521 tonnes.

items.stem: A country generates 400 TWh of electricity per year, of which 90 TWh is from renewables. Calculate the percentage from renewables.
Nia plans to investigate how the number of blades on a model wind turbine affects its power output. State three variables that must be controlled to make this a fair test.
items.answer: Any three of: wind speed from the fan (same setting and distance); blade size, shape and angle; the same generator and resistor; time for speed to stabilise (30 s)
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 3: wind speed from the fan (same setting and distance) – power depends strongly on wind speed; blade size, shape and angle – affect the force on blades; the same generator and resistor – affect the output; time for speed to stabilise (30 s) – output must be steady. The independent or dependent variable scores 0.

items.stem: A 40% efficient power station takes in 1000 MW. Calculate the power wasted and state where most of it goes.
items.answer: 600 MW; mostly as heat in cooling water and flue gases
items.markingKey: M1 useful = 400 MW; M1 wasted = 1000 − 400; A1 600 MW; B1 thermal energy in cooling water/surroundings.

items.stem:
Lars analysed data on the share of electricity generated from wind and solar worldwide in different years (three data sources).

Year | Share from wind and solar / %: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
2010 | 1.6 | 1.6 | 1.6
2013 | 2.3 | 2.3 | 2.4
2016 | 3.6 | 3.5 | 3.6
2019 | 5.6 | 5.4 | 5.3
2022 | 8.5 | 8.3 | 8.1

Calculate the percentage change in the mean share from wind and solar between 2010 and 2022.
items.markingKey: M1 means 1.60 and 8.30; M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100; A1 +418.7% (increase).

items.stem: A 2 MW solar farm produced 7884 MWh in a year. Calculate its capacity factor (1 year = 8760 h) and suggest why it is well below 100%.
items.answer: 45%; it produces nothing at night and less on cloudy days and in winter
items.markingKey: M1 maximum = 2 × 8760 = 17520 MWh; M1 7884 ÷ 17520 × 100; A1 45%; B1 night/cloud/season.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "Building more hydroelectric dams is the best way to provide clean electricity."
items.answer: Hydroelectricity is valuable where sites are suitable and impacts are managed, but cannot meet all needs.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: reliable, flexible, very efficient, long life; can store energy (pumped storage). Arguments against: floods valleys, displaces people, blocks fish migration; methane from rotting vegetation in reservoirs; suitable sites are limited. Supported judgement: Hydroelectricity is valuable where sites are suitable and impacts are managed, but cannot meet all needs.

items.stem: Rafael plans an investigation into how the energy-saving measures in a school affect its daily electricity use. Describe how the results should be recorded, processed and presented, and explain how the reliability and validity of the conclusion will be judged.
items.answer: Results table with the independent variable (measure in place (none; LED lighting; LED lighting plus automatic switch-off timers)) in the first column and repeat readings of the dependent variable with units in headings; calculate means (ignoring anomalies); plot a suitable graph of the mean dependent variable against the independent variable with a line of best fit; describe the trend and compare with the hypothesis; judge reliability from the spread of repeats and validity from how well variables were controlled.
items.markingKey: 1 table with IV, repeats and units; 1 means calculated, anomalies identified and excluded; 1 appropriate graph (line graph/scatter for continuous IV, bar chart for categorical) with line of best fit; 1 trend compared with hypothesis; 1 reliability (spread of repeats) and validity (controls) discussed.

items.stem: "Wind farms should be built in national parks if they are the windiest locations." Discuss.
items.answer: National parks should generally be protected; offshore and less sensitive windy sites should be prioritised.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: more electricity per turbine; helps tackle climate change, which also threatens parks. Arguments against: spoils protected landscapes and tourism; may harm wildlife; offshore sites are alternatives. Supported judgement: National parks should generally be protected; offshore and less sensitive windy sites should be prioritised. Markbands (8 marks): MYP criterion D (0-8, scaled): 7-8 explains thoroughly how the science is applied to address the issue, discusses and evaluates the implications (moral, ethical, social, economic, political, cultural or environmental), and documents sources consistently; 5-6 explains and discusses; 3-4 outlines; 1-2 states.

items.stem: Diego investigated how the speed of rotation of a model generator affects the output voltage. The method had this weakness: the speed drifted while readings were taken. Evaluate how this weakness affects the validity of the results and suggest an improvement to the method.
items.answer: use a motor speed controller and record only when the speed sensor shows a steady value
items.markingKey: 1 identifies how the weakness introduces error or an uncontrolled variable; 1 states the effect on the results/conclusion; 1-2 a specific, practical improvement: use a motor speed controller and record only when the speed sensor shows a steady value

items.stem: Which resource can respond fastest to a sudden increase in demand?
items.answer: Pumped-storage hydroelectricity
items.markingKey: B. Within seconds to minutes.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A structure that condenses steam back into water by transferring thermal energy to the air"?
items.answer: cooling tower
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of cooling tower.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "energy poverty"?
options: The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by an activity, product or person, in CO₂ equivalent
The variation in output of resources such as wind and solar that depend on weather and time of day
Lack of access to modern energy services such as electricity and clean cooking fuels
An energy resource that is replenished naturally on a human timescale, e.g. solar, wind, hydro, tidal, geothermal, biomass
items.answer: Lack of access to modern energy services such as electricity and clean cooking fuels
items.markingKey: C. "energy poverty" is lack of access to modern energy services such as electricity and clean cooking fuels.

items.stem: Explain the difference between wind power and solar power.
items.answer: Wind power uses moving air to turn turbines, works day and night but varies with wind speed; solar power uses photovoltaic cells (or heat), only works in daylight and varies with cloud cover and season.
items.markingKey: Wind power uses moving air to turn turbines, works day and night but varies with wind speed; solar power uses photovoltaic cells (or heat), only works in daylight and varies with cloud cover and season. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Rafael writes: "Power stations produce energy." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Power stations transfer energy from one store (chemical, nuclear, kinetic) into electrical energy; they do not create energy.
items.markingKey: Power stations transfer energy from one store (chemical, nuclear, kinetic) into electrical energy; they do not create energy. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "Switching to renewables only matters in rich countries." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Emissions from all countries affect the climate, and many developing countries have excellent renewable resources and fast-growing demand.
items.markingKey: Emissions from all countries affect the climate, and many developing countries have excellent renewable resources and fast-growing demand. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "Renewable resources have no environmental impact." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: They affect landscapes, wildlife, land use and need materials such as metals for turbines and panels.
items.markingKey: They affect landscapes, wildlife, land use and need materials such as metals for turbines and panels. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why CHP schemes increase the overall efficiency of a power station.
items.answer: Waste heat that would be released to the air or river is used to heat buildings, so a greater share of the fuel’s energy is useful.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Waste heat that would be released to the air or river is used to heat buildings, so a greater share of the fuel’s energy is useful. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between energy conservation and energy efficiency.
items.answer: Energy efficiency is doing the same task with less energy (LED bulbs); energy conservation is choosing to use less energy (switching lights off).
items.markingKey: Energy efficiency is doing the same task with less energy (LED bulbs); energy conservation is choosing to use less energy (switching lights off). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
Chloé measured the output of a small solar panel at different times of day (three sunny days).

Hours after sunrise / h | Power output / W: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
1 | 12.5 | 13.1 | 12.5
3 | 32.6 | 30.7 | 31.2
6 | 42.3 | 45.0 | 45.8
9 | 31.2 | 31.2 | 31.3
11 | 12.7 | 12.7 | 13.2

Calculate the mean power output when the hours after sunrise was 9 h.
items.markingKey: M1 (31.2 + 31.2 + 31.3) ÷ 3; A1 31.23 W (unit and sensible precision).

items.stem:
Sofia compared the efficiency of power stations commissioned in different decades using published data (three stations per decade).

Year commissioned | Efficiency / %: Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 3
1960 | 24 | 24 | 24
1975 | 32 | 32 | 31
1990 | 39 | 37 | 39
2005 | 43 | 44 | 46
2020 | 50 | 53 | 50

Calculate the percentage change in the mean efficiency between 1960 and 2020.
items.markingKey: M1 means 24.0 and 51.0; M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100; A1 +112.5% (increase).

items.stem: Tomás plans to investigate how the energy-saving measures in a school affect its daily electricity use. State three variables that must be controlled to make this a fair test.
items.answer: Any three of: school days only (exclude weekends and holidays); season (similar weeks); same buildings and equipment; meter readings at the same time each day
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 3: school days only (exclude weekends and holidays) – occupancy changes use; season (similar weeks) – heating and lighting demand changes with season; same buildings and equipment – new equipment changes demand; meter readings at the same time each day – reading time affects daily totals. The independent or dependent variable scores 0.

items.stem: In an investigation into how the number of blades on a model wind turbine affects its power output, state the dependent variable and describe how Mateo should measure it.
items.answer: power output = V²/R across a fixed 10 Ω resistor
items.markingKey: 1 mark for naming the dependent variable, 1 mark for a valid measuring method/instrument with unit: power output = V²/R across a fixed 10 Ω resistor.

items.stem: Amara wants to find out how the speed of rotation of a model generator affects the output voltage. Write a focused research question for this investigation that names both the independent and the dependent variable.
items.answer: How does rotation rate of the generator shaft affect peak output voltage?
items.markingKey: 1 mark: names the independent variable (rotation rate of the generator shaft (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 revolutions per second)); 1 mark: names the measurable dependent variable (peak output voltage measured with a data logger) in a question form.

items.stem: Briefly describe Germany’s Energiewende and explain what it reveals about balancing an energy transition.
items.answer: Germany expanded wind and solar to over 40% of electricity and phased out nuclear in 2023, but relied on coal and gas for backup during the transition. Shows the challenges of intermittency, costs and policy trade-offs.
items.markingKey: Context (Germany expanded wind and solar to over 40% of electricity and phased out nuclear in 2023, but relied on coal and gas for backup during the transition.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Shows the challenges of intermittency, costs and policy trade-offs. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to balancing an energy transition.

Arguments against: floods valleys, displaces people, blocks fish migration; methane from rotting vegetation in reservoirs; suitable sites are limited. Supported judgement: Hydroelectricity is valuable where sites are suitable and impacts are managed, but cannot meet all needs.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim: "Every household should install solar panels."
items.answer: Household solar is valuable where suitable and affordable, supported by grants and storage, but large-scale renewables are also needed.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: cuts bills and emissions; uses roof space; reduces grid demand at midday. Arguments against: high upfront cost; not suitable for shaded or rented homes; output peaks when demand is low unless batteries are added. Supported judgement: Household solar is valuable where suitable and affordable, supported by grants and storage, but large-scale renewables are also needed.
